query: CREATE FUNCTION RESOURCES_WITH_PERMISSION_FOR_LOGIN_ID(login_id UUID, permission_name TEXT) RETURNS TABLE(id UUID, resource_type_id UUID, workspace_id UUID, created TIMESTAMPTZ, deleted TIMESTAMPTZ) AS $$ DECLARE local_permission_id UUID; local_client_type ACTOR_CLIENT_TYPE; local_login_type USER_LOGIN_TYPE; BEGIN /* Resolve permission name to ID */ SELECT permission.id INTO local_permission_id FROM permission WHERE name = permission_name;  IF local_permission_id IS NULL THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'Permission `%` not found', permission_name; END IF;  /* The kind of login decides where its grants come from, so only that kind's query runs. A login with no actor_client row matches no branch below and gets nothing. */ SELECT actor_client.actor_client_type, user_login.login_type INTO local_client_type, local_login_type FROM actor_client LEFT JOIN user_login ON user_login.login_id = actor_client.id WHERE actor_client.id = RESOURCES_WITH_PERMISSION_FOR_LOGIN_ID.login_id;  /* Each branch collects the workspaces its grants touch first and only reads those workspaces' resources. Scope covers a resource when it is the resource itself or its whole workspace — two OR terms, never IN (NULL semantics); a third term arrives when projects land. Tombstoned resources are nobody's, whatever the grants say. */ IF local_client_type = 'runner' THEN /* A runner holds no bindings. Its grants are fixed, and must match the map its token loads: read access across its own workspace, and view and edit on itself. Its actor_client row outlives it, so a deleted runner is turned away on its own row. */ RETURN QUERY SELECT resource.* FROM runner INNER JOIN resource ON resource.workspace_id = runner.workspace_id WHERE runner.id = RESOURCES_WITH_PERMISSION_FOR_LOGIN_ID.login_id AND runner.deleted IS NULL AND resource.deleted IS NULL AND (permission_name IN ('containerRegistryRepository::pull', 'containerRegistryRepository::view', 'deployment::view', 'domain::view', 'managedURL::view', 'secret::view') OR (permission_name IN ('runner::edit', 'runner::view') AND resource.id = runner.id)); ELSIF local_client_type = 'service_account' THEN /* A service account authenticates as itself, so one id is its login, its actor_client registration and its actor: there is no membership row to go through. */ RETURN QUERY WITH bindings AS (SELECT role_binding.workspace_id, role_binding.scope_id FROM service_account INNER JOIN role_binding ON role_binding.actor_id = service_account.id INNER JOIN role_permission ON role_permission.role_id = role_binding.role_id AND role_permission.permission_id = local_permission_id WHERE service_account.id = RESOURCES_WITH_PERMISSION_FOR_LOGIN_ID.login_id AND service_account.deleted IS NULL) SELECT resource.* FROM (SELECT DISTINCT bindings.workspace_id FROM bindings) AS candidate_workspaces INNER JOIN resource ON resource.workspace_id = candidate_workspaces.workspace_id WHERE resource.deleted IS NULL AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM bindings WHERE bindings.workspace_id = resource.workspace_id AND (bindings.scope_id = resource.id OR bindings.scope_id = bindings.workspace_id)); ELSIF local_login_type IN ('web_login', 'oauth_login') THEN RETURN QUERY /* Workspaces where this login's user has super admin access */ WITH super_admin_workspaces AS (SELECT workspace.id AS workspace_id FROM user_login INNER JOIN workspace ON workspace.super_admin_id = user_login.user_id WHERE user_login.login_id = RESOURCES_WITH_PERMISSION_FOR_LOGIN_ID.login_id), /* Bindings carrying this permission, through the user's membership */ bindings AS (SELECT role_binding.workspace_id, role_binding.scope_id FROM user_login INNER JOIN workspace_user ON workspace_user.user_id = user_login.user_id INNER JOIN role_binding ON role_binding.actor_id = workspace_user.actor_id INNER JOIN role_permission ON role_permission.role_id = role_binding.role_id AND role_permission.permission_id = local_permission_id WHERE user_login.login_id = RESOURCES_WITH_PERMISSION_FOR_LOGIN_ID.login_id) SELECT resource.* FROM (SELECT DISTINCT candidate.workspace_id FROM (SELECT super_admin_workspaces.workspace_id FROM super_admin_workspaces UNION ALL SELECT bindings.workspace_id FROM bindings) AS candidate(workspace_id)) AS candidate_workspaces INNER JOIN resource ON resource.workspace_id = candidate_workspaces.workspace_id WHERE /* The parenthesised disjunction matters: AND binds tighter than OR, so without it this would only narrow the super-admin arm. */ resource.deleted IS NULL AND (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM super_admin_workspaces WHERE super_admin_workspaces.workspace_id = resource.workspace_id) OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM bindings WHERE bindings.workspace_id = resource.workspace_id AND (bindings.scope_id = resource.id OR bindings.scope_id = bindings.workspace_id))); ELSIF local_login_type = 'api_token' THEN RETURN QUERY /* Workspaces where this token has super admin access */ WITH super_admin_workspaces AS (SELECT user_api_token_workspace_super_admin.workspace_id FROM user_api_token_workspace_super_admin WHERE user_api_token_workspace_super_admin.token_id = RESOURCES_WITH_PERMISSION_FOR_LOGIN_ID.login_id), /* An API token's declared ceiling: its own (permission, scope) rows */ token_ceiling AS (SELECT user_api_token_permission_binding.workspace_id, user_api_token_permission_binding.scope_id FROM user_api_token_permission_binding WHERE user_api_token_permission_binding.token_id = RESOURCES_WITH_PERMISSION_FOR_LOGIN_ID.login_id AND user_api_token_permission_binding.permission_id = local_permission_id), /* The token owner's own grants; effective = ceiling ∩ owner, intersected per resource below */ token_owner_grants AS (SELECT role_binding.workspace_id, role_binding.scope_id FROM user_api_token INNER JOIN workspace_user ON workspace_user.user_id = user_api_token.user_id INNER JOIN role_binding ON role_binding.actor_id = workspace_user.actor_id INNER JOIN role_permission ON role_permission.role_id = role_binding.role_id AND role_permission.permission_id = local_permission_id WHERE user_api_token.token_id = RESOURCES_WITH_PERMISSION_FOR_LOGIN_ID.login_id UNION ALL /* A super admin holds every permission in their workspace without holding any role binding, so a token they own is capped only by its own ceiling. Projecting the workspace id into scope_id reuses the "scope is the whole workspace" convention the filter below applies. */ SELECT workspace.id AS workspace_id, workspace.id AS scope_id FROM user_api_token INNER JOIN workspace ON workspace.super_admin_id = user_api_token.user_id WHERE user_api_token.token_id = RESOURCES_WITH_PERMISSION_FOR_LOGIN_ID.login_id) /* Every grant has to be within the ceiling, so the ceiling's workspaces are the only ones the owner's grants can reach */ SELECT resource.* FROM (SELECT DISTINCT candidate.workspace_id FROM (SELECT super_admin_workspaces.workspace_id FROM super_admin_workspaces UNION ALL SELECT token_ceiling.workspace_id FROM token_ceiling) AS candidate(workspace_id)) AS candidate_workspaces INNER JOIN resource ON resource.workspace_id = candidate_workspaces.workspace_id WHERE resource.deleted IS NULL AND (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM super_admin_workspaces WHERE super_admin_workspaces.workspace_id = resource.workspace_id) OR (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM token_ceiling WHERE token_ceiling.workspace_id = resource.workspace_id AND (token_ceiling.scope_id = resource.id OR token_ceiling.scope_id = token_ceiling.workspace_id)) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM token_owner_grants WHERE token_owner_grants.workspace_id = resource.workspace_id AND (token_owner_grants.scope_id = resource.id OR token_owner_grants.scope_id = token_owner_grants.workspace_id)))); END IF; END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
